cards.back: Something that can change in an investigation.
cards.say: variable. Something that can change in an investigation.

cards.back: The one thing you choose to change in a fair test.
cards.say: independent variable. The one thing you choose to change in a fair test.

cards.back: The thing you measure to see the effect of the change.
cards.say: dependent variable. The thing you measure to see the effect of the change.

cards.back: The things you keep the same so the test is fair.
cards.say: control variables. The things you keep the same so the test is fair.

cards.back: A test in which you change only one variable, measure one variable and keep everything else the same.
cards.say: fair test. A test in which you change only one variable, measure one variable and keep everything else the same.

cards.back: What you think will happen, together with a reason.
cards.say: prediction. What you think will happen, together with a reason.

cards.back: Noticing something using your senses or instruments.
cards.say: observation. Noticing something using your senses or instruments.

cards.back: To check the results are reliable and to spot any odd result.
cards.say: Why do we repeat measurements? To check the results are reliable and to spot any odd result.

cards.back: Results are reliable if you get about the same results when you repeat the test.
cards.say: reliable. Results are reliable if you get about the same results when you repeat the test.

cards.back: A measurement is accurate if it is close to the true value.
cards.say: accurate. A measurement is accurate if it is close to the true value.

cards.front: You test which paper towel absorbs most water. What do you change?
cards.back: The type of paper towel. This is the independent variable.
cards.say: You test which paper towel absorbs most water. What do you change? The type of paper towel. This is the independent variable.

cards.front: You test which paper towel absorbs most water. What do you measure?
cards.back: The amount of water each towel absorbs. This is the dependent variable.
cards.say: You test which paper towel absorbs most water. What do you measure? The amount of water each towel absorbs. This is the dependent variable.

cards.front: You test which paper towel absorbs most water. What must you keep the same?
cards.back: The size of the towel, the amount of water and the time it soaks.
cards.say: You test which paper towel absorbs most water. What must you keep the same? The size of the towel, the amount of water and the time it soaks.

cards.back: A statement of what your results show, which answers your question.
cards.say: conclusion. A statement of what your results show, which answers your question.

cards.back: The results and observations that support a conclusion.
cards.say: evidence. The results and observations that support a conclusion.

cards.front: Why should you change only one thing in a test?
cards.back: So you know that this one thing caused any difference you see in the results.
cards.say: Why should you change only one thing in a test? So you know that this one thing caused any difference you see in the results.

cards.back: A stopwatch or a timer.
cards.say: Which tool measures time? A stopwatch or a timer.

cards.front: Which tools measure temperature, volume and force?
cards.back: A thermometer, a measuring cylinder and a forcemeter.
cards.say: Which tools measure temperature, volume and force? A thermometer, a measuring cylinder and a forcemeter.

cards.back: A neat way to record measurements, with headings and units.
cards.say: results table. A neat way to record measurements, with headings and units.

cards.back: A result that does not fit the pattern. Check it and repeat the measurement.
cards.say: anomalous result. A result that does not fit the pattern. Check it and repeat the measurement.

cards.back: The average of the results. Add them up, then divide by how many there are.
cards.say: mean. The average of the results. Add them up, then divide by how many there are.

cards.front: What is the mean of 4, 6 and 8?
cards.back: Six. Four plus six plus eight is eighteen, and eighteen divided by three is six.
cards.say: What is the mean of 4, 6 and 8? Six. Four plus six plus eight is eighteen, and eighteen divided by three is six.

cards.front: A plant test gives one plant more light and more water than another. Is it fair?
cards.back: No. Two things were changed, so you cannot tell which one caused the difference.
cards.say: A plant test gives one plant more light and more water than another. Is it fair? No. Two things were changed, so you cannot tell which one caused the difference.

cards.front: Why should you use plant pots of the same size in a test?
cards.back: Pot size is a control variable and must be kept the same.
cards.say: Why should you use plant pots of the same size in a test? Pot size is a control variable and must be kept the same.
